title: Does the symbolic learner actually use signed axial-spin feedback?
hypothesis: The frozen R-051 learner sustains spin through signed axial-angular-velocity feedback rather than an effectively open-loop gait.

prediction.rationale: Baseline is the unchanged R-051 learner; reversing only its observed axial velocity should reduce frozen episode-level sustained success by at least 15 percentage points if this feedback drives its successes.

protocol.command: gpu run 'bash -lc "source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --study learner_axial_sign --manifest-seed 4400 --output-dir logs/pen_spin_learner_axial_sign_s4400"'
code_changes: Extend scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py with the declared --study and --output-dir interface, reusing the validated Isaac rollout and record paths.
Add learner_axial_sign to config/pen_spin_plateau_repair.yaml; resolve the frozen R-051 learner by recorded lineage and save its hash.

Audit computational dependence before simulation. For intervention episodes replace omega with omega - 2*(omega dot pen_axis)*pen_axis in policy observations, updating any redundant derived fields but not simulator state, rewards, orientation, hand state or timing.
Freeze the new development manifest before scoring: 32 paired unchanged/reversed episodes plus eight additional identity-transform reproducibility episodes; abort on reproducibility failure.

Reuse the established sustained-success rule and paired t interval. Unlike D-040/D-042, this isolates signed spin feedback in the symbolic learner rather than removing or delaying the expert's state channels.

falsified_by: A paired interval lying entirely above -0.15 refutes the predicted magnitude; an interval including zero supplies no evidence of a difference. A dependency audit proving that the learner never uses axial velocity directly refutes the proposed mechanism without simulator runs.

approval.note: This isolates signed axial-velocity dependence in the symbolic learner, unlike the decided expert-feedback interventions. post_hoc_drive_saturation.how: evaluated on the unchanged learner's in-play axial spin (env spin_rate, rad/s, equal to the learner's 5*obs projection); post hoc, not predeclared

lines: # Positive startup drive; excessive spin can reverse the stroke.

notes: Identity gate passes: the identity-wrapper repeat is bit-identical to the learner on all 32 cases.

Primary: axial-reversed minus learner = -0.031 [-0.176, +0.113] (4/32 vs 5/32; 2 wins, 3 losses, 27 ties). The predicted decrease of at least 0.15 is not shown; the interval is not entirely above -0.15, so by the predeclared rule this is not a refutation either: inconclusive on magnitude, with no evidence of any difference.
Reversal did not slow the pen: mean |spin| 7.39 vs 6.89 rad/s (per-episode means), drops 9 vs 8.

Mechanism (post hoc): the source reads the signed axial rate, but the selected parameters (spin_target 12.16 rad/s, speed_gain 0.81) put drive = 0.25 + 0.75 tanh(gain (target - spin)) in saturation: on the learner's own in-play steps the drive exceeds 0.99 on 94.6% of steps, and reversing the sign changes it by more than 0.05 on only 10.4%. The source audit establishes a code path, not an active feedback; in the visited range the spin law is effectively a fixed-amplitude, open-loop stroke.

The frozen state has spin_target 12.16 against the source's declared initial 8.0 (it is the state the R-046 prefix probe search selected and promoted; how that search moved it is not examined here). At 8.0 the drive would be unsaturated over much of the visited range, so the operating point, not the code path, decides whether the feedback is active; a static audit cannot see this.

verdicts.reasoning: Identity gate passed (bit-identical on 32/32). Predicted a decrease of at least 0.15; observed -0.031 [-0.176, +0.113] (4/32 vs 5/32, 27 ties). The predeclared refutation needs the interval entirely above -0.15 and its lower bound is -0.176, so neither the prediction nor its refutation is established; the interval includes zero. Post hoc, the reason the lever is weak is visible: the frozen parameters (spin_target 12.16, speed_gain 0.81) saturate the drive 0.25 + 0.75 tanh(gain (target - spin)) above 0.99 on 94.6% of the learner's in-play steps, and reversing the axial sign changes it by more than 0.05 on only 10.4% of steps. The source audit found a code path, but at its operating point the learner is effectively an open-loop fixed-amplitude stroke in axial spin; reversal also did not slow the pen (|spin| 7.39 vs 6.89).
verdicts.next_experiment: Treat the learner's spin as open loop when designing repair evidence (R-054). A sharper dependence test would set the operating point inside the unsaturated range (e.g. spin_target at its declared 8.0) or replace the measured axial rate with the target (zero error) rather than reversing it.

verdicts.reasoning: The unchanged baseline was measured: axial reversal produced 4/32 successes versus 5/32, giving paired_success_difference = -0.03125 [logs/pen_spin_learner_axial_sign_s4400/summary.json]. The 95% paired interval [-0.17559, +0.11309] includes zero, so there is no evidence of a difference; it also crosses -0.15, neither establishing nor refuting the predicted decrease of at least 0.15 against baseline [logs/pen_spin_learner_axial_sign_s4400/summary.json]. The identity control matched observations and outcomes on all 32 cases, supporting the comparison's reproducibility [logs/pen_spin_learner_axial_sign_s4400/summary.json]. The source audit establishes a signed axial-rate dependency, while the post hoc diagnostic reports drive above 0.99 on 94.6% of baseline in-play steps; neither establishes that this feedback causes sustained success or that an open-loop replacement would preserve it [logs/pen_spin_learner_axial_sign_s4400/source_audit.json] [logs/pen_spin_learner_axial_sign_s4400/summary.json].

history.note: Before any episode: (1) pen-spin manifests take one pool seed, so the 32 cases come from seed 4400 alone (4401-4431 never used, not recorded); (2) a case's outcome depends on its batch (D-035), so the identity-transform reproducibility control must rerun the whole 32-case batch, not 8 extra cases: 3 x 32 = 96 episodes; (3) the Isaac studies live in config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml (learner_axial_sign block), not the plateau-repair yaml. Source audit (lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/axial_sign.source_audit): the learner reads obj_angvel and drives speed_gain*(spin_target - spin) with spin = omega . axis. Seed 4400 recorded in the ledger.

direction: Continue researching the single-step exploration pipeline with plateau-triggered trace repair, extended to pen spinning on the Shadow Hand (Isaac Lab Isaac-ShadowHandSpin-Stage{1,2,3}-Direct-v0, vendored in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin; 157-d full obs, 20-d action, 60 Hz, 360-step episodes). Expert demonstrations: first try a hand-written scripted spinning controller; also search online for an existing trained pen-spinning policy; if neither qualifies, train an RL expert (rsl_rl PPO on the box). No budget ceiling on GPU hours or LLM calls. Known gaps to turn into questions: the env's spin_rate is roll about the pen's own long axis (not end-over-end twirl), success is per step with no episode rule, and the pipeline (manifests, obs schema, runner, records) is MetaWorld-only today. Debug issues, improve the pipeline, and turn unexpected findings into concrete research questions; document results and limitations.

advisor.reasoning: This isolates signed axial-velocity dependence in the symbolic learner, unlike the decided expert-feedback interventions. Its weakest point is that sign reversal tests dependence under an observation shift, not proof of a stabilizing feedback law. The dependency audit and identity-control gate justify 72 episodes and zero LLM calls using scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/pen_spin_plateau_repair.yaml. Falsified_by: the predicted paired_success_difference decrease of at least 0.15 against unchanged R-051 is refuted by an interval entirely above -0.15, or by an audit establishing no signed axial-velocity dependence.

implementer.reasoning: Agree. The source audit already shows dependence: spin = omega . axis feeds speed_gain*(spin_target - spin), so the sign reversal is a live lever. I will implement it as a learner_axial_sign study beside learner_recovery in config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml (that file holds the Isaac studies; the plateau-repair yaml is for the LLM pipeline) with the same Gate-1 identity repeat.
